policy.title: Epidural Steroid Injections for Pain Management

root.label: Initial epidural steroid injection is medically reasonable and necessary

children.label: Qualifying condition supported by history, exam and concordant imaging
Radiculopathy, radicular pain or neurogenic claudication from disc herniation, osteophyte or severe DDD producing foraminal or central stenosis
Imaging concordant with the qualifying condition
Severity documented with a baseline objective scale
Pain greatly impacts quality of life or function
Objective pain scale or functional assessment recorded at baseline
Four weeks of pain and failed or intolerable conservative care
Pain duration of at least 4 weeks
Failure of 4 weeks of noninvasive conservative care, or inability to tolerate it
Acute herpes zoster refractory to conservative management (4-week wait not required)
Enrolled in active rehabilitation, home exercise or functional restoration program
No contraindication (spinal or systemic infection, cord/conus/cauda equina compression, cancer risk)
No more than 4 ESI sessions in this spinal region in the past 12 months

Pain Management Consultation
Date: 09/06/2026
Patient: [NAME_1] [NAME_1], 67-year-old male

Subjective:
Reports low back pain radiating to the right leg for 22 weeks. Function: unable to stand long enough to cook a meal, has stopped driving because of the pain.

Objective:
No red flags: afebrile, no unexplained weight loss, no history of malignancy, no saddle anesthesia.

Assessment:
Assessment: right lumbar radiculopathy at L5-S1 due to disc herniation with foraminal stenosis.

Plan:
Baseline NRS prior to any intervention: 9/10. Epidural steroid injection history: 2 lumbar injections in the past 12 months (10/16/2025, 01/02/2026). Continues the daily home exercise program taught in PT. Will consider further interventional options and continue conservative management with physical therapy and pain control.

events.rationale: The most recent pain management note (09/06/2026) explicitly states 'No red flags: afebrile, no unexplained weight loss, no history of malignancy, no saddle anesthesia,' ruling out infection, cancer risk, and compressive lesions as contraindications within days of the request.

citations.quote: No red flags: afebrile, no unexplained weight loss, no history of malignancy, no saddle anesthesia.

events.text: While the documentation confirms only 2 prior injections in the past 12 months, it completely omits the clinical response, percentage of pain relief, and duration of relief obtained from the 10/16/2025 and 01/02/2026 injections. Evidence of efficacy from prior injections is required to justify subsequent epidural steroid injections.

The cited quote for physical therapy (04/16/2026 to 05/14/2026) lacks specific details regarding the frequency of sessions and the actual modalities used. Furthermore, there is no documentation of a trial of conservative pharmacological management (e.g., NSAIDs, membrane stabilizers) to constitute a comprehensive conservative care plan.

The baseline NRS score of 9/10 does not specify whether it measures the axial low back pain or the radicular leg pain. For an epidural steroid injection targeting radiculopathy, the objective pain scale must specifically reflect the severity of the radicular symptoms.

The documentation notes 'afebrile' and 'no red flags', but fails to explicitly rule out a local skin infection at the planned injection site or coagulopathy/bleeding disorders, which are standard absolute contraindications for epidural steroid injections.

The statement 'Continues the daily home exercise program taught in PT' is vague. It lacks details on the specific exercises, duration, and objective evidence of patient compliance to verify active participation in a functional restoration program.

events.rebuttal: The chart does not explicitly document absence of local skin infection at the injection site or absence of coagulopathy/bleeding disorders. This documentation is missing.
